A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAA/RR formulations and DOHJ-PPO work. Their readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original grid-world simulations and Hopper/F16 experiments, including learned trajectories, success rates, and achievement times in Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds SafetyGym, HalfCheetah, and stochastic-dynamics evaluations in Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: The objectives, state augmentation, value decompositions, Bellman/GAE updates, and PPO procedure are retained. Concurrent training and coupled resets emphasized in v2 Section 7.2 already appear in v1 Appendix F; the DO-HJ-PPO to DOHJ-PPO renaming does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 retains grid-world, Hopper, and F16 coverage while adding SafetyGym Point and HalfCheetah RAA/RR tasks. It also evaluates HalfCheetah under stochastic transition conditions absent from v1.

E2.justification: Compared with v1's CPPO, RA, and DSTL comparisons, v2 Figure 4 adds evaluated PPO, PPO-LAG, RCPPO, RESPO, MORL, SPARSE, P2BPO, and LOGBAR baselines on retained tasks. The RR figures show one C-PPO entry instead of separately displaying three CPPO variants, although their definitions remain in Appendix G.

E3.justification: V2 adds partial success as an evaluation metric and a controlled noise protocol: Gaussian perturbations to velocities/angular velocities at scales 0, 0.5, 1, and 2, with learning curves evaluated over 256 trajectories. The ordinary comparisons retain 1,000 evaluation trajectories. Newly disclosed budgets for retained experiments do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: Section 8.3 and Figure 5 add a dedicated noise-sensitivity study of both HalfCheetah tasks against three leading baselines per task, testing the stochastic approximation's robustness. V1 contains no corresponding sweep. The qualitative observation about removing coupled resets was already present in v1 Appendix F.

E5.justification: V2 Section 8.3 newly specifies three seeds and reports maximum learning curves over them; v1 states no seed count. This adds run-count and aggregation reporting without establishing increased runs for retained experiments. The new curves do not report across-seed uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 4–6 substantially expand success, partial-success, and achievement-time results across tasks and comparators. Figure 5 adds findings that the RAA advantage disappears at the highest noise level while RR performance remains stronger. New speed comparisons also show exceptions to universal superiority: SPARSE has fewer mean steps than DOHJ-PPO in Hopper-RAA.

T1.justification: The original decomposition proofs are retained, but v2 adds Theorem 4 and its contraction/monotonicity proof relating stochastic-policy SRABE values to the optimal discounted RA value. Appendix A.1 adds a direct RAA Bellman derivation, and Appendix L adds formal temporal-logic semantics and counterexamples distinguishing predicate decomposition from optimal-value decomposition.

C1.justification: The central contributions—RAA/RR formulations, decomposition results, and DOHJ-PPO—remain unchanged. V2's conclusion adds claims of rigorous justification for the stochastic-policy formulation and empirical robustness to certain stochastic dynamics, extending the stated contribution within the existing framework.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes stochastic-policy justification from unresolved guarantees under stochastic dynamics, discusses noncommuting expectations and extrema, and identifies high-noise limitations. It also develops applicability boundaries for larger logical compositions and explains why temporal-logic predicate algebra does not directly yield optimal-control decompositions.

D1.justification: V2 Tables 2–3 newly disclose parallel-environment counts, rollout lengths, total timesteps, scan steps, update epochs, and minibatches for retained experiments. Appendices J–K and Tables 4–5 document rewards, obstacles, initialization, and training settings for the added environments. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V1's brief related-work discussion becomes an extensive treatment of constrained/MORL, goal-conditioned RL, temporal logic, generalized objectives, and HJ methods. V2 adds numerous substantive citations, including Wang et al. (2020), Cui and Yu (2023), and Tang et al. (2025), and sharpens its distinction from temporal-logic decomposition.

P1.justification: V2 adds a separate introduction and contribution list, substantially rewrites the motivation and related work, expands formulation explanations, and organizes experiments into dedicated subsections. Algorithm and policy-gradient material moves into the appendix, producing substantial narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, enlarging retained illustrations. V2 adds an environment montage and noise-learning curves, restructures success comparisons, separates achievement-time plots into Appendix Figure 6, and expands or adds hyperparameter tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow empirical validation, supplies an explicit justification for the stochastic-policy surrogate, and fills important training-budget and rollout disclosures. These improve the paper's evidential basis and reproducibility. Maximum-over-three-seed noise curves and the blanket fewest-steps claim, contradicted by some Figure 6 comparisons, temper but do not outweigh these gains.
